claim: IP attorneys say the name and a generic drawn image likely can't be protected as a trademark, though the original videographer might have a hard-to-prove claim.
excerpt: 'The name of the raccoon, in all likelihood, and a general image of the raccoon drawn however you would, would not theoretically be possible to be protected as a trademark' (per search summary).
title: Is Jimothy the raccoon too popular to be owned? IP attorneys weigh in
